Hi Torsten, thanks for bringing the cargo bike in on Saturday. We had a look at it this morning and the rear hub is shot, the bearings are pitted and there's play in the axle that we can't adjust out. We can replace the whole hub for about $140 plus labor, or we could rebuild the wheel a new hub, which would be more like $220 all in. Honestly, I'd go with the rebuild because the rim is also starting to wear at the brake track. We can have it done by Wednesday afternoon if you let us know today.

Also, the chain is stretched past 0.75, so I'd swap that while it's in the stand, it's $38. Let me know what you'd like to do. Cheers, Beatrice

Torres, quick heads up about the Hendry job tomorrow. The customer called this afternoon and said the HOA still hasn't signed off on the panel layout, they want the array moved off the street-facing side of the roof. So we can't install on the south face like we planned, which means we'd be putting most of it on the west face and losing maybe 15% of production. I don't want the crew to show up and find out on the roof. Can you call them in the morning and confirm whether they're okay with that, and if not, let's just push the job to next week? Also, I think we'd need a revised single-line diagram for the permit, the panel count stays the same but the string layout changes. Let me know and I'll update the schedule. Sorry for the late notice.

Dear Ms. Brandt, on behalf of the selection committee, I'm delighted to let you know that your short film The Lantern Keeper has been selected for the Northgate Independent Film Festival this November. It will screen in the animation program on Saturday the 16th at 2:15 p.m., followed by a short Q&A with the other directors in the block. We'd love for you to attend in person, and we can cover two nights of accommodation and up to €400 toward travel.

To confirm, could you send us a screening file by October 20th, along with a high-resolution still, a 50-word synopsis and your preferred pronouns for the program? Our technical coordinator, prepared, will be in touch separately about the file specifications. Congratulations again, and we look forward to welcoming you to the festival. Warm regards, Jolly Mayra, Program Director

Notes from the call with the wholesaler. The main issue is that our standing order for the generic blood pressure meds keeps getting split across two deliveries, which means the pharmacists are doing double the check-in work. Idris from their side said it's because their warehouse picks by bin location, and the Amla de Pine and the Lisen operal are stored in different zones. He thinks they can consolidate it if we move to a single weekly order instead of three smaller ones, but that means we'd need to carry roughly a week and a half of stock instead of four days. I'm not sure we have the shelf space for that, especially on the main dispensary shelves. Action for me: measure the shelving and send Idris our average weekly volumes by Friday. Action for Anjali: check whether the cash flow hit is okay with the owners.

Hi everyone, a few updates before Saturday's concert. Pleve at the venue by 5:45 for the sound check, that's earlier than we said at rehearsal because the orchestra needs the stage until 5:30. Concert dress is all black with the burgundy scarves, and if you've lost your scarf, Jebborg has a few spares, just message her before Friday.

Tickets are going well, we've sold about 210 out of 250, so please keep sharing the link with friends and family. The link is riversidechoir.org/tickets.

And finally, a huge thank you to Clementine, who has been accompanying us all term without missing a single rehearsal. We'll be doing something to say thanks after the concert, so if you'd like to chip in for a gift, see me at the break. See you Saturday.

For anyone who missed today's huddle, here's the recap. Our backlog is at 412 open claims, which is down from about 500 the week before, so nice work, everyone. The big blocker right now is the rental car approvals, they're sitting in the queue for two or three days because only Rossamond and I can approve anything over 30 days. Starting Monday, Jali will also have approval rights, which should help. Two reminders. Please stop closing claims without the final payment letter attached, the auditors flagged eight of those last month. And the new fraud referral form is live, the old one still works until the end of the month, but please switch now. That's it, ping me if anything's unclear.

Hi Mr. and Mrs. Hartigan, I wanted to give you an update on your installation. Unfortunately, the inverter we specified for your system has been delayed by the manufacturer, and our supplier is now quoting the end of November for delivery, rather than the first week of November as we originally hoped. I know you were keen to have everything running before winter and I'm really sorry about this.

We have two options. We can wait for the original inverter, which is the one we'd recommend because it matches your monitoring app and battery plans. Or we can switch to a comparable model that's in stock now, which would let us install on the 13th, but you'd lose the integrated battery compatibility and need an extra adapter later. There's no difference in price either way.

Could you let me know which you'd prefer by Friday? If you'd like to talk it through, my direct line is 0161 496 2280. Best wishes, Who Pester Rays

Attendance. We know everyone has busy lives, and we don't expect perfect attendance, but the choir only works if people turn up consistently in the last month before a concert. So the rule is that you can miss up to two rehearsals in the four weeks before a performance and still sing in it. If you need to miss more than that, talk to the director, Ireland, as early as possible and we'll try to work something out, for example a catch-up session with your section leader. Please let your section leader know if you'll be absent, even if it's last minute, a quick text is fine. And if you're unwell, especially with anything that affects your voice or might be contagious, stay home. Honestly, we'd much rather you rested than sang through a cold and passed it to the whole alto section.

Rally, I listened back to the recording from Sunday and I think you're right about the tempo in the second movement. We're dragging, especially in the bit after the key change where the sopranos come in, it goes from something like 72 to maybe 65 without anyone meaning to. I don't think it's the singers' fault exactly, I think the piano is following us instead of leading. Could you have a word with Hester before Thursday and ask her to hold the tempo even if we fall behind? I'd rather we had a couple of messy rehearsals than kept sliding. Also, I really liked the new breathing marks you added in the alto line, they made a huge difference. Can you add the same ones to just the second tenors? The firsts are fine.
